market_note: No roster change vs June 4: same 10 names, with GULF holding the #1 CUS slot after crossing THB 1tn market cap on a THB 140bn ($4.3bn) AI data-center plan plus FTSE inclusion. Tone is cautious-defensive — SET slipped ~1.3% to 1,572.50 on thin THB 69bn turnover amid Delta-led selling, a ~THB 5bn FTSE-revision outflow, Mideast/Hormuz risk and a hawkish Fed; dividend-rich banks and lower-oil importers cushion the downside.

names.name: Gulf Development
names.driver: Billionaire Sarath Ratanavadi's THB 140bn ($4.3bn) plan to 10x data-center capacity to ~2,000MW (Microsoft/Google/Singtel deals) plus FTSE inclusion is pulling in foreign capital.
names.risk: Stretched valuation after the trillion-baht run leaves the stock vulnerable to AI-capex sentiment swings and any delay in data-center ramp or financing.
names.guide: Management guides to double-digit 2026 revenue growth with limited Mideast impact; brokers expect continued upside into H2 on data-center and FTSE flows.
names.latest_quarter: Q1 2026: net profit ฿9,117m, +39% YoY; core profit ฿9,326m (+43%, record); revenue ฿39,041m (+21%); beat.
names.cash: Low yield (~1-2%); heavy capex, leverage rising on DC build-out; profit boosted by AIS stake

names.name: Advanced Info Service
names.driver: 5G subscribers rose to 18.5m and mobile service revenue grew 7.6% YoY, with broadband and enterprise/digital adding a defensive, dividend-backed growth leg.
names.risk: Heavy ฿30-35bn capex and a maturing, two-player mobile market cap pricing power and free-cash upside.
names.guide: Management reaffirmed full-year guidance (in line) with ฿30-35bn capex to extend 5G (>95% coverage) and fixed broadband.
names.latest_quarter: Q1 2026: net profit ฿13.49bn, +28% YoY; revenue ฿58.19bn (+3.4%); EBITDA +7.1%; in line/beat.
names.cash: Solid ~3-4% yield, strong recurring cash flow, defensive balance sheet

names.name: Airports of Thailand
names.driver: Tourism recovery continues (FY25 ~126m pax, +11%) and the new international PSC hike to ฿1,120 from mid-June lifts per-passenger revenue.
names.risk: Mideast conflict and soft Chinese/regional demand forced a FY26 pax-target cut to 126m (from 135m), capping the recovery.
names.guide: AOT trimmed FY26 passenger guidance to ~126m but analysts still frame it as a top tourism-recovery infrastructure play on the PSC uplift.
names.latest_quarter: 1H FY2026 (Oct-Mar): traffic growth ~4-7% across major airports (Suvarnabhumi +4.4%, Don Mueang +7.5%); earnings recovering but pressured by demand softness.
names.cash: Low yield (~1-2%); capex-heavy on terminal expansion; strong franchise cash flows

names.name: CP All
names.driver: 7-Eleven same-store sales and traffic rose on recovering Chinese tourism and post-election domestic mobility, and a ฿7.5bn buyback signals confidence.
names.risk: Soft Thai consumer spending, high household debt and elevated group leverage weigh on the multiple.
names.guide: Management guides to continued store expansion (16,084 stores) and margin gains; brokers positive on consumption/tourism leverage.
names.latest_quarter: Q1 2026: net profit ฿9,118m, +20.2% YoY; total revenue ฿267,672m (+5.8%); CVS sales +7.0%; beat.

names.name: Krung Thai Bank
names.driver: Best-in-peer NIM expansion and ~28% non-interest income growth underpin a ~7.7% dividend yield, drawing broker upgrades (DBSV Buy, TP ฿38.50).
names.risk: BoT policy rate at 1% and falling sector NIM/loan growth (-1.1% YoY) cap earnings; asset-quality risk if GDP (1.5%) disappoints.
names.guide: Brokers (DBSV ฿38.50, Krungsri ฿38) rate Buy, expecting a sustained ~7% yield and long-term dividend growth.
names.latest_quarter: Q1 2026: net profit roughly flat-to-modestly-up YoY (sector profit growth <1%); resilient vs peers on NIM and fee income; in line.
names.cash: High ~7.7% dividend yield; ~40% payout policy; strong capital

names.name: Kasikornbank
names.driver: Net profit grew 6.35% YoY on a 28% jump in non-interest income, and a sector-leading ~7.1% dividend yield (฿32/sh cumulative) is fueling a banking-stock rally.
names.risk: Lower policy rate compresses NIM (~2.91%, -45bps) and weak loan demand limits top-line growth amid a soft economy.
names.guide: Management/brokers point to robust dividend payouts and fee-income momentum offsetting NIM pressure; constructive on payout-driven re-rating.
names.latest_quarter: Q1 2026: net profit ฿14,667m, +6.35% YoY; non-interest income ฿17,564m (+28.4%); broadly in line.
names.cash: High ~7.1% dividend yield; strong CAR and provisioning buffers

names.name: Bangkok Bank
names.driver: Deep-value, well-capitalized lender with a ~5.9% yield and the highest corporate-loan gearing to any Thai capex/data-center investment upcycle.
names.risk: Q1 net profit fell ~12.9% YoY on lower operating income, the weakest of the big banks, as NIM and loan growth contract.
names.guide: Analysts keep a value/dividend stance; recovery hinges on loan-growth stabilization and non-interest income rebuilding.
names.latest_quarter: Q1 2026: net profit ฿10,994m, -12.9% YoY; lower operating income; miss.
names.cash: ~5.9% dividend yield; lowest P/BV among majors, very strong capital

names.name: Central Pattana
names.sector: Real Estate (Retail REITs / Real Estate Management & Development)
names.driver: Record-high rental revenue and 62% rental gross margin on rising mall traffic, plus a ฿110bn 2026-2030 'Future-Led Ecosystem' expansion pipeline.
names.risk: Large multi-year capex and reliance on Thai consumption/tourism expose returns to a domestic-demand slowdown.
names.guide: Management guides to continued retail-led growth and new mall openings (Central Chanthaburi); analysts constructive on tourism recovery.
names.latest_quarter: Q1 2026: net profit ฿4,971m, +18% YoY; total revenue ฿13,352m; record margins; beat.
names.cash: ~2-3% yield; mixed-use cash flows fund expansion; moderate leverage

names.name: Bangkok Dusit Medical Services
names.sector: Health Care (Health Care Providers & Services / Hospitals)
names.driver: Largest Thai private hospital network (60 hospitals) with stable domestic demand and ~10% underlying foreign-patient growth ex-conflict markets.
names.risk: Lower Cambodian and Middle East patient volumes from regional conflict dragged revenue flat and profit -7% YoY, pressuring margins.
names.guide: Brokers (e.g. DBSV) flag soft near-term earnings on weak top line/margins but see core medical demand intact; defensive hold.
names.latest_quarter: Q1 2026: net profit ฿4,058m, -7% YoY; revenue ฿28,554m (flat); miss.
names.cash: ~2% yield; defensive, low-leverage healthcare balance sheet

names.name: Minor International
names.driver: Strong RevPAR across Europe (~74% of revenue), Thailand and Maldives drove core profit +189% YoY, with robust Q2 European advance bookings.
names.risk: High seasonal Q1 losses, FX and European/macro sensitivity plus elevated leverage make earnings volatile.
names.guide: Management sees continued momentum on robust European advance bookings and is advancing REIT/asset-monetization plans to cut debt.
names.latest_quarter: Q1 2026: core net profit ฿145m, +189% YoY; reported net profit ฿649m (+56%); core revenue ฿38,488m (+5%); beat.
names.cash: Low ~1-2% yield; deleveraging via REIT monetization; seasonal Q1 cash drag
